summary: Added docs/DEV_PLANS.md, a new dev-plans doc capturing the decided multi-account Docker migration architecture (stateless-tick scheduling, per-strategy job granularity, DB-as-source-of-truth, DB schema decisions, logging split, Alembic migration convention, accounts.yml import mapping) and its current build status, so this is tracked in-repo instead of only in Claude memory. Linked it from README.md's docs/ listing.
Broadened the code-change-log skill's scope to explicitly cover ANY repo change (docs, config, scripts, the skill itself), not just source code -- per user request that all repo changes get logged.

Added a new skill, trading-analysis, per explicit user request: an on-demand diagnostic that reads a strategy's live/paper trading logs (reports/logs/<STRATEGY>/, per strategy-logging's layout), resolves which of possibly several coexisting runner implementations is actually live (this repo is mid-migration from legacy single-account launchd runners to a DB-driven webapp/runner.py coordinator for both S007 and S009), filters out test-pollution artifacts (a traceback whose frames include a tests/ path is a test run hitting a module-level production logger, not a real incident -- this concretely happened this same session with scripts/s007_tick.py's run_cycle()), and reasons from the strategy's OWN signal-function fields (in_window/day_done/filtered/direction/n_desired/resolved-ghost-trades for S007, target book vs broker positions for S009) to give an explicit bug-vs-normal-behavior verdict when there is no open position, with a plain-language verdict plus the technical log evidence backing it. Strategy-agnostic by design, not hardcoded to S007. Supports two scopes: today's session (default) vs a wider multi-day 'in principle, does this bot reliably behave correctly' check across events-<date>.jsonl history, driven by the user's stated goal of validating strategy automation correctness in general, not just curiosity about one session. Triggered by 'проанализируй торговлю <NNN/name>' and similar phrasing, for any strategy. Registered it in orchestrator/SKILL.md's skill catalog (the project's single routing table) so it's picked up the same way as every other domain skill.

Added the Docker/Ofelia scaffold for the DB-driven multi-account runner (docs/DEV_PLANS.md's 'one job per STRATEGY' design): a single worker image (Dockerfile + requirements-docker.txt, split from the research-only requirements.txt) runs `python -m webapp.runner --strategy <NAME>` per Ofelia job-run tick; only S007 is wired into a schedule so far ('* 10-16 * * 1-5', mirroring scripts/s007_tick.py's in_session() window). Verified end-to-end on this machine's Podman (not Docker) setup: image builds cleanly after loosening the cryptography/pyOpenSSL/service-identity pins (the exact local-venv trio was mutually unresolvable from a clean install), a one-off container run against the real demo account round-tripped through the bind-mounted data/app.db and reports/logs correctly, and Ofelia registers/runs the labeled job. Podman-machine specific fix documented in docker-compose.yml: bind-mount /run/podman/podman.sock (not the macOS-side /var/run/docker.sock forward) read-write, plus security_opt label=disable to clear an SELinux AVC denial on Fedora CoreOS (enforcing by default) that otherwise blocks the socket connect even as container root. Did not touch webapp/runner.py's S007-only dispatch, S009, or the legacy launchd job -- scoped to standing up the framework itself.
